title: Wake of an actuator-surface rotor without and with wings
description: Steady RANS runs of the repository's actuator-surface case (rotor only and four wing strips) on the supplied mesh, ported to OpenFOAM v2412. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 2. Velocity deficit behind an actuator-surface rotor alone (top) and with four wing strips (bottom); brighter blue is slower flow, amber lines are streamlines from the actuator ends.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Coherent-structure colouring of Ahmed-body tracks
description: Shake-the-Box particle tracks measured behind the Ahmed body (TU Delft Open Jet Facility), coloured with the Python CSC implementation; the CSC mode is selected against streamwise vorticity from the same measurements. Sparse and dense random subsets of the near-wake tracks, seen along the stream. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 3. Particle tracks measured behind an Ahmed body, seen along the stream, with sparse (left) and dense (right) seeding; red tracks belong to the trailing vortex.
credit: Measurements: TU Delft Aerodynamics Laboratories; analysis and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Voronoi neighbour-persistence coherence in a double gyre
description: The repository's dense double-gyre example (784 tracers, 101 frames over t = 0-20, seed 7) analysed with its Python implementation of the Voronoi method. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 4. Voronoi cells of 784 double-gyre tracers coloured by neighbour persistence (the sign is arbitrary), with amber trails of their recent motion.
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Vortex wake of an elastically mounted cylinder
description: Two-dimensional URANS (k-omega SST) re-run in OpenFOAM v2412 of a cylinder free to move across the flow, with the mass ratio, spring stiffness and damping of Martins & Avila (2019, Marine Structures 65); coarser than the published simulations and shown across the span. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 5. Vortex cores behind an elastically mounted cylinder, coloured by spanwise vorticity (teal clockwise, red anticlockwise). Coarse 2D OpenFOAM re-run with the study's mass, stiffness and damping; not the published simulations.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: 37-member truss before and after sizing
description: The 37-member benchmark of the paper (Fig. 6) sized with a Python re-implementation of the linear indirect method, compared at equal mass with a truss of uniform member areas. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 6. The 37-member benchmark truss at equal mass with uniform areas (top) and after sizing (bottom); tube thickness follows area, colour is stress over admissible stress (teal compression, red tension).
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Effective potential and an orbit of the restricted three-body problem
description: Earth-Moon-like mass fraction (0.0121505856) and Jacobi constant 3.2, as in the repository defaults; orbit started at x = 0.30 on y = 0 and integrated with the repository's DOP853 integrator. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 7. Effective potential of the Earth–Moon system in the rotating frame, with one orbit (amber), the zero-velocity curve and the five Lagrange points; height compressed logarithmically.
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: OpenFOAM cell-centre samples and their regular-grid resampling
description: Plane x = 12 of the bundled OpenFOAM snapshot (actuator-surface wake, time 429) read with fluidfoam: cell centres within 0.03 of the plane (left), and streamwise velocity resampled onto a 0.06 grid with the repository's RBF settings (right). Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 8. One wake plane of the bundled snapshot: OpenFOAM cell centres sized by mesh spacing (left) and the same velocity deficit on a regular grid (right).
credit: Processing and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Lid-driven cavity at Re = 1000
description: Steady lid-driven cavity flow at Re = 1000 computed with the repository's projection solver on a 192 x 192 grid; centreline velocities checked against Ghia, Ghia & Shin (1982). Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 9. Steady cavity flow at Re = 1000: the texture follows the flow direction, colour is vorticity (teal clockwise, red anticlockwise), with eddies in both lower corners.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Three-bladed rotor and its helical lifting-line wake
description: Rotor of examples/three_blade_rotor.py (radius 50 m, root 10 m, tip-speed ratio 8, DU95W180 polars, 22 panels per blade, wake convected at U(1 - a) with a = 1/3; CT = 0.64, CP = 0.46) solved with the repository's vectorised lifting-line solver. Trailing filaments carrying at least 4% of pi U^2/(N_b Omega) are drawn to two radii downstream. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 10. Three-bladed rotor (radius 50 m, tip-speed ratio 8) and its helical wake to two radii downstream; filaments are coloured by the circulation they trail, red at the tips and teal at the roots.
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Reverse von Kármán street behind a plunging flat plate
description: Flat plate of 10 panels plunging at reduced frequency k = 1 and amplitude 0.2 chord at zero mean angle of attack, 520 time steps, solved with the repository's numba-accelerated vortex panel solver; wake vortices drawn as Gaussian blobs (radius 0.07 chord) of their vorticity in a frame that follows the plate along the stream. Render style after the OpenONDA tutorial figures (black background, thesis colour maps, LaTeX overlay); reproduce with scripts/render/make_figure.sh in the repository.
caption: Figure 11. Wake of a flat plate plunging at reduced frequency k = 1 (amplitude 0.2 chord): shed vortices, drawn as blobs of their vorticity, form a reverse von Kármán street.
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins
